title: UX Signal Library and Accessibility Mapping for Cost Rollout States
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a compact, labelled "signal" token library that represents cost and rollout states across the Redwood Console. The library will include color tokens, iconography, microcopy snippets, and an accessibility contrast matrix specifically targeted at: cost anomalies, budget thresholds, canary/rollout states, fallback model routing, and quota exhaustion. Deliverables: Figma component library, token spec JSON for engineering, copy guide for status text, and a short handoff doc with priority tradeoffs for dark/light themes.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file contains a dedicated 'Signals' page with tokens grouped by semantic purpose (Cost, Rollout, Reliability, Quota).
Every token has an exported name, hex/RGBA values, intended use case example, and contrast ratio measured against background in both light and dark themes.
4 interactive component variants implemented in Figma: Cost Badge, Rollout Rail, Quota Toast, and Signal Legend. Each variant includes responsive behavior and spacing tokens.
A token spec JSON (flat name/value pairs) uploaded to the design-system repo with clear mapping to the runtime config keys used by frontend (example keys included).
Accessibility sign-off from the accessibility reviewer (contrast & screen-reader copy checks) documented in comments.
Hand-off checklist completed with links to PRD, engineering intake, and a short demo recording.
Cross-team review acknowledgement from PM and Eng (comments captured).
comments: 2026-02-11 — Ava Chen: Initial kickoff meeting notes. Aligned scope with PM Diego Martinez: focus first on Cost and Rollout axes, defer model-variant tokens to follow-up. Agreed to keep token palette compact (6 primary signals).
2026-02-18 — Priya Nair: Prototype v1 uploaded to Figma (Signals page). Added Cost Badge and Rollout Rail components. Asked Eng for token key naming preferences — tag: @Liam O'Connor

2026-02-20 — Liam O'Connor: Engineering feedback: prefer hyphenated keys (signal-cost-warning) and separate semantic tokens from theme tokens. Also request sample token JSON for the runtime team. Added dependency: ENG-7012 for theming adapter work.

2026-02-25 — Ava Chen: Accessibility pass started with Sofia Ruiz. Early finding: our yellow warning variant fails 4.5:1 on 14px body on light theme. Two options discussed: increase weight of tone or add an outline. Decided to try slightly darker tone and fallback outline for small labels.
2026-03-02 — Priya Nair: Updated components with outline fallback. Added microcopy guide: short (6-7 chars) vs expanded (20-30 chars) for badges and tooltips. Linked examples in Figma.

2026-03-05 — Diego Martinez (PM): Reviewed and suggested adding a 'degraded' signal for graceful fallback states when a lower-cost model is used. Marked as high information priority for Dedicated customers.
2026-03-09 — Priya Nair: Added 'degraded' and 'canary' signals; created a small interaction prototype for rollout rails to show canary percentages and auto-fallback hints. Shared link in attachments.

2026-03-11 — Sofia Ruiz (Accessibility): Final contrast report attached in comments. All tokens meet 4.5:1 for body text except 'cost-muted' which is approved only for decorative usage. Recommended ARIA label patterns for signal badges.

2026-03-12 — Ava Chen: Engineering handoff PR drafted (see gist). Next steps: coordinate with ENG-7012 for runtime mapping and schedule a paired review 2026-03-16. Added sub-issue DES-993312 for copy localization review.
notes: Trade-offs: keeping palette small reduces cognitive load but requires clear microcopy and iconography to disambiguate similar tones.
Implementation gap: frontend currently expects color tokens in camelCase; we will provide both hyphenated and camelCase variants in the spec to ease adoption.
Localization: badges have two copy flavors; short labels required for narrow UIs — flagged for translation review (DES-993312).
